introduction: On this fifth Sunday of Lent, God promises through Ezekiel to open the graves of his people and put his Spirit in them. In the Gospel, Jesus weeps at the tomb of his friend Lazarus, says, I am the resurrection and the life, and calls Lazarus out of the tomb. Paul tells us that the Spirit who raised Jesus will give life to our mortal bodies. Where catechumens celebrate the third scrutiny, we pray for them.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, with the Lord there is mercy and fullness of redemption. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may proclaim Christ, the resurrection and the life, to all who live in the shadow of death. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the catechumens: that Christ may unbind them from sin and raise them to new life in Baptism. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are grieving: that they may know that Jesus weeps with them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the sick and the dying: that they may believe in Christ, who gives eternal life. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that Christ may call us out of whatever tomb holds us. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, your Son wept for his friend and called him from the tomb. Raise us from sin to new life, and bring us with the catechumens to the joy of Easter. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: I am the resurrection and the life
reflection.body:
Ezekiel speaks to a people in exile who feel as good as dead. God promises: "Behold, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves, my people." And: "I will put my Spirit in you, and you will live."

The Gospel tells how Jesus does exactly that. His friend Lazarus is ill. His sisters, Martha and Mary, send word: "Lord, behold, he for whom you have great affection is sick." John tells us, "Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus." Yet Jesus waits, and by the time he arrives, Lazarus has been in the tomb four days.

Martha comes to meet him with honest grief: "Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn't have died." Jesus tells her, "Your brother will rise again," and then he says the great words: "I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me will still live, even if he dies." He asks her, "Do you believe this?" And Martha makes a profession of faith: "Yes, Lord. I have come to believe that you are the Christ, God's Son."

When Mary comes weeping, and Jesus sees the mourners, "he groaned in the spirit and was troubled." Then comes the shortest verse in the Bible: "Jesus wept." The Lord of life shares our grief.

At the tomb, Jesus prays to his Father and cries out, "Lazarus, come out!" The dead man comes out, still wrapped in burial cloths. Jesus says, "Free him, and let him go."

Paul tells us that the same Spirit "who raised up Jesus from the dead" lives in us and "will also give life to your mortal bodies."

Today we pray for the catechumens. This week, bring Jesus your own tomb: a sin, a grief, a fear. Hear him call you out, and let others help unbind you.
